COURT’S OR JUDGES’S ORDERS
WPCRL No. 1299 of 2025
Hon’ble Rakesh Thapliyal, J. 
1. Mr. Suhaas Ratna Joshi and Ms. Bhavya Sharma, 
learned counsel for the petitioner.
2. Mr. J.S. Virk, learned Deputy A.G. with Mr. 
Bhaskar Chandra Joshi, learned A.G.A. and Mrs. Sweta 
Badola Dobhal, learned Brief Holder for the State.
3. The statutory committee refused to release the 
petitioner simply for the reason that he is a convict of a 
heinous crime of murder of a minor child for ransom.
4. Learned counsel for the petitioner argued that the 
reasoning of the committee is completely contrary to 
Rule 5 of 2022 policy i.e. Uttarakhand State (For 
Sentence Pardon/Premature Release of Convicted 
Prisoners Punished with Sentence of Imprisonment for 
Life by the Court) Permanent Policy, 2022 as notified 
on 25.11.2022.
5. In support of his argument he gives reference of 
the judgment passed by the Division Bench in the case 
of Suo Moto PIL: In the matter of Premature release of 
the convicts vs. Principal Secretary, Home, 
Government of Uttarakhand and Others i.e. WPPIL 
No. 50 of 2024 dated 27.09.2024. On perusal of 
paragraph 18, which contains the list of 34 inmates 
including the petitioner mentioned at S.No. 11 reveals 
that out of 34 inmates only one case of Sundar Singh 
S/o Har Singh, which is seen at S.No. 25 fall under the 
prohibited category in terms of Rule 5(iv) of 2022 
Policy.
6. In this judgment of Division Bench comes to the 
conclusion that the committee has rightly not 
recommended Sundar Singh for premature release and 
then further observed that since 33 inmates do not fall 
under the prohibited category as per Rule 5 of 2022 
Policy, hence, they are eligible for premature release. 
Finally the Division Bench directed the committee to 
consider the matter.
7. The question is once the Division Bench clearly 
observed that 33 inmates including the petitioner does  not fall under the prohibited category and found to be 
eligible for premature release how the committee took 
a contrary view by taking into consideration that the 
petitioner was involved in a heinous crime. Prima-facie 
the reasoning as given by the committee is contrary to 
the judgment passed by the Division Bench of this 
court as well as contrary to Rule 5(iv) of 2022 Policy.
8. Mr. Virk pointed out that the provisions has been 
incorporated under the Jail Manual, which is in 
consonance with 2022 policy i.e. Uttarakhand Jail 
Manual, 2023.
9. Let the committee take a fresh decision strictly in 
the light of the observation of the Division Bench as 
well in terms of Rule 5 of the Policy as well as Jail 
Manual of 2023 and then apprise to this court by 
27.02.2026.
10. List this matter on 27.02.2026.
 
 (Rakesh Thapliyal, J.)
 24.02.2026
PR

Hon’ble Ravindra Maithani, J.
Hon’ble Siddhartha Sah, J.
Mr. Sharang Dhulia (through video 
conferencing), Mr. Suhaas Ratna Joshi, Mr. 
Sandeep Adhikari, Mr. Ankush Kumar Tyagi, 
Mr. Pragya Prakash Upadhyay, Ms. Manisha 
Bhandari, Advocates Mr. Himanshu Singh 
Jolly, Advocate, holding brief of Mr. Aditya 
Singh, Advocate for the petitioners.
Mr. J.S. Virk, A.A.G. for the State.
Mr. I.D. Paliwal, Advocate for the 
respondent no.3 in WPCRL No. 920 of 2026.
Mr. Navnish Negi, Advocate for the 
informant in WPPIL No. 50 of 2024.
These are the cases pertaining to 
premature release of the convicts in accordance 
with the State Policy of 2022.
It is the grievance of the petitioners that 
despite being eligible for premature release, 
their cases have not been considered for 
premature release.
On 25.05.2026, when this matter was 
taken up, on behalf of the State Government, it 
was argued that committee considering the 
remission had held meeting on 22.05.2026 
and had recommended eight persons for 
premature release. On that date, it was 
assured that there are 40 other cases, 
including the cases of the petitioners which 
would be taken up in near future.
On 25.05.2026, under instructions, on 
behalf of the State, learned State counsel gave 
an assurance that cases of the petitioners for 
premature release shall be considered within  two weeks.
Today, learned State counsel would 
submit that the names of the petitioners were 
considered, but only two names were 
recommended for premature release and 
names of Nihal Singh, Pawan and Sukhdev 
Singh have not been considered for premature 
release.
Learned State counsel tendered the 
instructions which he received. Let it be taken 
on record.
The proceeding records that in view of the 
report of the Superintendent of Police and the 
District Magistrate, the cases of Nihal Singh, 
Pawan and Sukhdev Singh were not 
recommended for premature release.
The Court wanted to know from learned 
State counsel, as to under what clause of the 
Policy of 2022, such recommendation has a 
final bearing on the premature release of the 
convicts.
Learned State counsel submits that it is 
not in the Policy.
The question is that the premature 
release is to be ensured in accordance with the 
Policy of 2022, which is not done in the case? 
Why? Who is responsible for it?
The Court contemplated to seek response 
from the Committee for such action, which 
appears to be dehors the Policy of 2022. But, 
then learned State counsel submits that he 
may be given 24 hours time to convey the 
correct legal position so that the cases may be 
considered in accordance with the Policy of 
2022 and the settled law.
List on 11.06.2026 at 04:00 p.m.
(Siddhartha Sah, J.) (Ravindra Maithani, J.) 
 10.06.2026
Jitendra

This bunch of petitions has been filed by the convicts for 
their premature release. In fact, certain directions were issued 
in WPPIL No. 50 of 2024, wherein, in Para No.24, a table was 
also given, which reveals that, in fact, in 71 cases, this Court 
has directed for consideration of premature release, and in 45  cases, the report was awaited.
On 12.08.2026, this Court had requested learned State 
Counsel to submit the list of 71 and 45 inmates, along with 
their status with regard to whom directions were given by this 
Court in WPPIL No.50 of 2024 on 27.09.2024.
The reports are not being placed. It is causing avoidable 
delay in disposing of these writ petitions. 
In Para No.24 of the judgment dated 27.09.2024, in 
WPPIL No.50 of 2024, the Coordinate Bench of this Court has, 
inter alia, noted that, “...The decision of the Government has 
to be lawful and fair as per Article 14 of the Constitution. 
During the pendency of this writ petition, following data 
has been considered:-
Total inmates considered 
for release
167 + 37 = 204
Inmates recommended for 
release by the Committee
74
Direction given by this 
Court for consideration for 
premature release
38 + 33 = 71
Reports awaited with 
regard to the 
consideration of 
premature release
45
Inmate(s) died in custody 01
The Court wanted to know as to what is the detail of 71 
and 45 inmates with regard to whom directions were given for 
their consideration of premature release, as well as with regard 
to whom the reports were awaited, respectively.
This status is not being submitted by learned State 
Counsel.
The Court directs the Principal Secretary, Home,
Government of Uttarakhand, to file an affidavit, categorically 
giving details of all those 71 and 45 inmates, who have been 
referred to in Para No.24 of the judgment dated 27.09.2024 by 
the Coordinate Bench of this Court in WPPIL No.50 of 2024.
The details shall include as to whether their matter has 
been considered? And if so, what action has been taken, and 
when the action was taken? The report shall be in the following 
format:-
S.No. Name 
of the 
inmate
Offence 
under 
which 
sentenced
The 
sentence 
imposed
The 
Court 
which 
imposed 
the 
sentence
Whether
the case 
was 
considered 
for 
premature 
release? If 
so, when?
What 
decision 
was taken 
on 
premature 
release? This affidavit shall be filed within two weeks from today.
List this matter for hearing on 07.09.2026.
Let a copy of this order be forwarded to the Principal 
Secretary, Home, Government of Uttarakhand, forthwith for 
compliance. 
(Siddhartha Sah, J.) (Ravindra Maithani J.) 
 19.08.2026
